label: rem:descartes-knot-eigenbasis-derivation
title: Derivation of knot-eigenbasis completeness
html:
Completeness of the knot-type eigenbasis follows in four steps.

  1. (Iwahori--Hecke algebra instantiation.) The Descartes condition sets the genus g(M_0) = 4; the volume axiom, independently, sets the gauge group to \mathrm{SU}_q(2), of rank 1 and with two-dimensional fundamental object. The R-matrix of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) (R-matrix braiding) supplies a braiding c_{V,V} on \mathbf{C} with eigenvalues q and -q^{-1}. The quotient by the quadratic relation (c_{V,V} - q)(c_{V,V} + q^{-1}) = 0 yields the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(q) acting on V^{\otimes n}.
  2. (Schur--Weyl decomposition.) The Descartes condition demands q not be a root of unity (via 6 \in R^{\times} and non-degeneracy of the Frobenius form). Consequently, H_n(q) is semisimple (Jimbo's theorem). The q-Schur--Weyl decomposition (knot eigenbasis completeness(1)) applies: every V^{\otimes n} decomposes into irreducible summands labelled by two-part partitions \lambda \vdash n.
  3. (Braid representation.) The faithful representation \rho_3 \colon B_3 \to \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbf{C}}(V^{\otimes 3}) (braid-group structure(1)) extends to \rho_n \colon B_n \to \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbf{C}}(V^{\otimes n}) for all n via braid action on tensor products. The Markov trace on the Iwahori--Hecke algebra tower detects every irreducible summand.
  4. (Completeness.) By the combining theorem (knot eigenbasis completeness), the three inputs—Schur--Weyl decomposition, Alexander surjectivity, and Markov trace detection—yield a complete knot-type eigenbasis for the algebraic direct limit V_{\mathrm{phys}} = \varinjlim V^{\otimes n}. A finite categorical trace over knot-labelled summands replaces the Feynman path integral.
